chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Maghrib and 'Isha prayers are combined with one Adhan and two Iqamahs, and do not pray anything in between them.
And he said, "Thus the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) prayed."
ai.seo_question: How are the Maghrib and Isha prayers combined during Hajj at Muzdalifah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the specific ritual protocol for *Jam' al-Qasr* (combining and shortening prayers) at Muzdalifah, emphasizing a single Adhan with two distinct Iqamahs to maintain the structural integrity of each prayer unit. It serves as a key evidentiary basis in Shia fiqh for the validity of this combined prayer during the Hajj rites, directly linking the Imam's instruction to the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad. This practice highlights the flexibility within the ritual framework to accommodate the physical demands of the pilgrimage while preserving the distinct identity of Maghrib and 'Isha.
